doc: Where a vendored binding and a real file of this repository disagree (fbl-implementation Requirement 12). Each entry is checked by the real-file suite: an unlisted disagreement fails, and so does a listed one that has changed or no longer occurs. Never edit a vendored binding, skip a file or weaken an assertion instead.

divergences.reason: mindmap.fbl's branch relation selects /map/**/node/node, the same entries the node element rule selects. FBL section 5.1 gives an entry to the first matching rule, elements before relations, so the node rule claims every node and no branch is ever read; the nesting is still there as each node's parent. Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: express branches as the node rule's containment only, or let a relation rule read an entry an element rule also claims.

divergences.observed: 2 layout entries name no element: variable:Test, variable:variable1

divergences.observed: Connection: the binding lacks 4 (bothgone, fromnowhere, noends, tonowhere)
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the timeline module's findings corpus, written to hold dangling connection ends on purpose. The difference is between two bindings: the vendored example reads a connection as an FBL relation, and FBL section 5.4 reads no relation whose end names no element; the module's own binding (timeline.fbl) reads a connection as an element whose from and to are references, so every connection is read and the definition reports the dangling end (timeline-disl-fbl finding B2). Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: let a relation rule read an entry whose end does not resolve, so a host can report it.

divergences.observed: Subchart: the binding lacks 1 (sub:charts/nochart)
divergences.reason: charts/nochart holds only readme.txt, which no file rule selects. helm-chart.fbl's file rules select files, and the folder body hands the plugin only what they select (FBL sections 10.2 and 11.2), so a directory under charts/ that holds no selected file is no entry the plugin can see: the reader drew it as a subchart. This is gap 3 of definitions/diagrams/helm-chart.md (findings B4 and B5), which the module answers with directory entries of its own (HelmFolderEntries, handed to the folder body beside the binding); this cross-check gives the folder body the binding alone, so the gap shows. Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: entries: "all" on a file rule, so a binding can select a directory as an entry.

divergences.observed: Relationship: the binding adds 1 (web->api)
divergences.reason: 'web->api', written without spaces around the arrow, is a relationship to Structurizr and to structurizr.lark, whose WORD holds no '->'; C4Parser splits a statement at white space and reads '->' only as a word of its own, so it reads no relationship there. The binding is right; the module is lenient elsewhere (finding B6) but not here.

divergences.observed: offset 101: '}' is invalid without a matching open.
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the Databricks module's parity corpus (databricks-disl-fbl task 1), written not to be JSON on purpose (finding B7). FBL refuses to read the body, which is the right answer for it; the sentence is the one .NET's JSON reader gives, which the json family reports without its line and position (B-29), where the module reports databricks.unparseable with YamlDotNet's message. The parity transcript freezes what the module does with it today.

divergences.observed: Resource: the binding lacks 1 (aliased)
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the Databricks module's parity corpus (databricks-disl-fbl task 1), written to hold an anchor, an alias and a merge key (finding B5). The job 'aliased' writes its tasks as the alias *shared_tasks. Since task 11 the module reads the file through its own binding and, under the reading adopted for B5, reads no entry through the alias either, so its job 'aliased' has no tasks, as databricks-job.fbl's has none. What remains is the bundle's side: the module reads every job resource as a Resource, and databricks-job.fbl, which reads a job file, reads no resource for the aliased job.

divergences.observed: Flow: the binding adds 1 (a->b) | Node: the binding adds 2 (a, b)
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the Sankey module's parity corpus (sankey-disl-fbl task 1), written to hold a key written twice in one mapping (finding B9). YamlDotNet refuses the document, and the module asks it whether a body is YAML before it reads the binding's reading (SankeyBody), so the module reads nothing of it; FBL section 7.4 binds the first of the two and reports fbl.duplicate-key, so the binding reads every node and flow. Q4 keeps the module's answer for this conversion: a duplicated key still makes the document unreadable.

divergences.observed: Flow: the binding lacks 1 (a->b); the binding adds 1 (->) | Node: the binding lacks 2 (a, b)
divergences.reason: The fixture is one of the Sankey module's parity corpus (sankey-disl-fbl task 1), written with its nodes and its flow as flow mappings (- {id: a, name: A}), the second shape of finding B16. YamlDotNet reads them as mappings like any other; to FBL's YAML family a flow mapping is one value whose members CEL sees and no key slot binds (FBL section 4.3), so the binding's slots read no id and neither end. The module reads such an entry's values from the binding's computed written attribute, the written text of every member (SankeyReader, sankey-disl-fbl task 10), so it draws them as before. That FBL binds no member of a flow mapping is gap 11 of the definition's companion, definition/sankey.md, a candidate change for etalii.adp.

divergences.observed: User.name: The new name would not read back from the text.
divergences.reason: The person's name is written bare ('Person User'), a WORD. The binding writes a value as it is inside the token it replaces (FBL 0.11 section 4.9), so 'User edited' would be two words, and the set is refused because the entry would not read back with it (section 6.4). C4Parser writes a quoted name. Candidate follow-up for etalii.adp: a slot that requotes a bare value it cannot write as one word (the 'requote' of FBL 0.15's escape).

divergences.observed: View: the binding lacks 1 (containers)
divergences.reason: The software system's block is never closed, so the '}' meant for the model closes it and 'views {' stands inside the model, where the grammar reads it as an unbound statement; its container view is then no view of the body, and the model and the workspace are reported fbl.unclosed-block (the structurizr-recover-nested fixture). C4Parser counts no braces and reads the view. Both keep the bytes; the binding reads the text as Structurizr would.

divergences.observed: Parent: the binding lacks 1 (api in b)
divergences.reason: With '!identifiers hierarchical' both containers are 'api'; FBL reads ids flat, so the second 'api' is a duplicate id (std.duplicateId) and the first, in a, is the element the id names. C4Parser keeps both. Hierarchical identifiers stay unsupported (c4-disl-fbl task 14).

divergences.observed: Include: the binding lacks 1 (https:); the binding adds 1 (https://example.com/model.dsl)
divergences.reason: '!include https://example.com/model.dsl': structurizr.lark reads the URL as one word, the longest match, and the binding's include rule its whole path; C4Parser takes '//' as the start of a comment wherever it stands and reports the path as 'https:'. The binding is right.
